title: Etale–pro-etale cohomology comparison for arbitrary abelian sheaves
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] of its small sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and every integer $i\geq0$, the canonical cohomology pullback is an isomorphism of abelian groups $$H^i(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(T_{\mathrm{proet}},
u_T^{-1}F).$$ Here cohomology means right derived global sections and $
u_T^{-1}$ is the abelian-sheaf inverse image [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. There is no torsion, finiteness, constructibility, or fixed coefficient ring assumption.

proof.text: Put $L=\nu_T^{-1}$ and $G=\nu_{T,*}$ on abelian sheaves. By [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections], for every etale object $U\to T$ the comparison unit on underlying sheaves of sets identifies $F(U)$ with $(LF)(U)$. The abelian inverse image and its unit have these underlying set functors and unit, by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3). Thus $\eta_F:F\to GLF$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves: each component is a bijective group homomorphism, whose inverse is a group homomorphism. For each morphism $a:F\to F'$, naturality of the cited sections identification gives $(GLa)_U\circ\eta_F(U)=\eta_{F'}(U)\circ a_U$ for every etale $U$; hence the unit isomorphisms are natural in $F$.

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ in abelian etale sheaves, using the enough-injectives and cohomology conventions of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1)-(2). Exactness of $L$ from [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact] makes $LF\to LI^\bullet$ an exact augmented resolution. Each $LI^n$ is $G$-acyclic by [lem-cbc-abelian-comparison-injective-acyclicity]. Apply clause (2) of [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] to $v=G$ and this resolution: $R^qG(LF)$ is computed by $H^q(GLI^\bullet)$. The natural unit of step 1 identifies the complex $I^\bullet$ with $GLI^\bullet$, commuting with every differential by unit naturality. Hence $R^qG(LF)=0$ for $q>0$, since $I^\bullet$ resolves $F$. This uses only an ordinary resolution in degrees at least zero, with no boundedness or finiteness assumption on $F$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-leray-degenerate] to the morphism $\nu_T$ and the pro-etale abelian sheaf $A=LF$, with $V$ the terminal etale object $T\to T$. The inclusion sends it to the terminal pro-etale object. The hypothesis $R^qG(A)=0$ for $q>0$ is exactly step 2. Thus for each $i\geq0$ the edge map $e_A^i:H^i(T_{\mathrm{et}},GLF)\to H^i(T_{\mathrm{proet}},LF)$ is an isomorphism. By the cited statement, it is specifically $H^i(\varepsilon_{LF})\circ\nu_T^*$, not an unspecified isomorphism. Compose this edge isomorphism with $H^i(\eta_F)$, an isomorphism by step 1.

proof.text:
The preceding composite is the canonical pullback on $F$. Indeed the coefficient naturality of [lem-weil-pbc-site-cohomology-pullback] (2), applied to $\eta_F:F	o GLF$, gives $
u_T^*\circ H^i(\eta_F)=H^i(L\eta_F)\circ
u_T^*$. Consequently $e_{LF}^i\circ H^i(\eta_F)=H^i(\varepsilon_{LF}\circ L\eta_F)\circ
u_T^*=
u_T^*$, by the triangle identity for $L\dashv G$ of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Since both factors on the left are isomorphisms, the pullback is an isomorphism. This also checks $i=0$, where the map is the unit on sections; no change of coefficient category has occurred.
